conviction_note: Revenue is pre-announced so the only new information on 1 Sep is everything below the revenue line and the balance sheet; a hard share-count identity (398.83m = 336.33m at 31 Dec 2025 + the 62.5m January shares, i.e. zero issuance since) lets me bound H1 cash at roughly $131m before burn against a ~$102m term loan maturing 31 Dec 2026 and a $300m buyback mandate the market has been pricing since 30 June, so I take about a third of the 12.0% implied move to the downside against a +16.8% five-day run-up and call-heavy option open interest (P/C OI 0.25).

findings.finding: Rezolve has issued no new shares since the January 2026 raise (398.83m shares outstanding today = 336,327,587 at 31 Dec 2025 + the 62,500,000 sold at $4.00 on 21 Jan 2026, to the share), which lets H1 cash be bounded from the outside: $111.1m at 31 Dec 2025 + $250m gross January proceeds - $230m paid all-cash for Reward Loyalty on 10 Feb 2026 = at most ~$131m before H1 operating burn (FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was -$59m) and before the ~$102m Crownpeak/Monroe term loan that matures 31 Dec 2026 - so only a small single-digit-percent fraction of the $300m repurchase mandate is actually fundable, and the H1 balance sheet is where that arithmetic first becomes public.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no consensus balance sheet for this name: it is a semi-annual foreign private issuer with zero recoverable earnings-reaction history, five analysts all at Strong Buy with a $10.50 target, and every sell-side preview anchored on the pre-announced $127m revenue and the $360m guide. If the market had done this subtraction, the stock would not have run 16.8% in five days into the print on partnership press releases, front-expiry put/call open interest would not be 0.25, and the 30 June buyback mandate would not still be treated as a $300m bid. The share-count identity that makes the bound tight (zero issuance since January) is the piece nobody has cross-checked, and it is exactly what removes the 'they must have raised more' escape hatch.
findings.independence: Cash of $111.1m at 31 Dec 2025 and adjusted EBITDA of -$59m come from the FY2025 results release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526130487/rzlv-ex99_1.htm, 2026-03-30); the 336,327,587 share count at 31 Dec 2025 from the 20-F (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/RZLV/20-f-rezolve-ai-plc-files-annual-report-foreign-issuer-7842680420d4.html, 2026-03-30, snippet_only for the exact figure); the $230m all-cash, 'no financing, no equity issuance' funding of Reward from https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/rezolve-ai-acquires-reward-loyalty-for-230-million-in-allcash-deal-93CH-4496476 (2026-02-13); the $250m at $4.00 from https://rezolve.com/press-releases/rezolve-ai-closes-250-million-oversubscribed-financing-enters-2026-with-one-of-the-strongest-balance-sheets-in-ai-commerce/ (2026-01-26).

findings.finding: The UK statutory accounts of Rezolve AI PLC (company 14573691) for the year ended 31 December 2025 were due at Companies House by 30 June 2026 and are still not filed as of 31 August 2026 - the register shows the last accounts on file as the period ending 31 December 2024 and flags accounts overdue - even though the company published an 'Annual Report and Accounts 2025' as Exhibit 99.2 to a 6-K on 30 March 2026, and its shareholders only passed the resolution covering auditor appointment on a resolution filed 22 July 2026, three weeks after the statutory deadline.
findings.why_not_priced: No US aggregator, wire or terminal reads the UK register for a Nasdaq-listed issuer, and the company's own defence against Fuzzy Panda and Grizzly was explicitly that the shorts 'disregard audited financials'. If this were priced, the two published short theses would have led with it - a UK PLC two months delinquent on its statutory accounts while telling the market its audited numbers vindicate it is a free headline neither short has used, which is direct evidence it has not circulated. It matters into a print because the H1 figures are management-account based and unreviewed, and a delinquent statutory audit is the cheapest available reason to discount them.
findings.independence: Corroborated within the same register by the 22 Jul 2026 'Resolutions' entry covering auditor appointment and share-purchase authority on the filing history page (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/14573691/filing-history), and by the fact that the FY2025 accounts were already published to the SEC on 2026-03-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526130487/2025_results_pr_and_ar_6.htm), so the delay is not an absence of accounts.

findings.finding: Rezolve AI PLC - the listed parent itself, not a US subsidiary - registered a charge in favour of Monroe Capital Management Advisors LLC created 22 December 2025 and still outstanding, plus a second outstanding charge in favour of Crownpeak Technology Holdings LLC created 19 January 2026, meaning the ~$102m of Crownpeak term loans maturing 31 December 2026 (Term SOFR + 5.50%) are secured at the top of the group; the $300m buyback in turn requires a UK court-sanctioned capital reduction, expected mid-September, in which secured creditors get a formal creditor-protection say.
findings.why_not_priced: The SEC disclosure frames the Monroe debt as loans 'assumed' with the acquired entity; the UK charges register is what shows the plc granted security over itself, and nothing in the US filing chain, the press releases or the two short reports mentions it. If the market had joined it to the capital reduction, the stock would not have rallied on the 30 June buyback mandate as if $300m were unconditional - the court route with a secured lender due to be repaid four months later is a live gate on both the timing and the size, and the 1 September call is the first place management has to speak to it after the mandate vote.
findings.independence: The term-loan amount, 31 December 2026 maturity and the Monroe amended-and-restated credit agreement are established separately from the December 2025 6-K reproduction at https://www.streetinsider.com/SEC+Filings/Form+6-K+REZOLVE+AI+PLC+For:+Dec+01/25680399.html (2025-12-01, snippet_only); the mid-September court-approval condition is from the AGM release at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000119312526291046/rzlv-ex99_1.htm (2026-06-30). Partially overlaps finding 1 on the same debt maturity.

findings.finding: Rezolve took a $63.3m impairment in FY2025 on its SQD (Subsquid) token holdings and told investors continued volatility could force further impairments; SQD traded around a $0.0627 low in January 2026 and was capped by a $0.056-$0.058 resistance zone by June 2026, so the H1 2026 accounts most likely carry another digital-asset writedown into a net loss line the market has no estimate for, because only the revenue line was pre-announced.
findings.why_not_priced: The 27 July pre-announcement gave revenue only and explicitly nothing on gross margin, EBITDA, cash or the bottom line, so there is no published loss estimate for H1 at all; a crypto token's H1 price path is not an input any RZLV preview contains. If this were priced you would see it discussed alongside the $127m headline rather than the ARR and partnership copy that has driven the last five sessions. I could not establish the residual carrying value of the token position after the 2025 writedown, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate small.
findings.independence: SQD price levels are snippet_only from https://coinmarketcap.com/cmc-ai/subsquid/price-analysis/ (accessed 2026-08-31) and are a different source class entirely from the SEC disclosure of the impairment; independent of findings 1-3.

searched_and_found_nothing: Reward Loyalty UK Limited's group accounts for the year ended 30 April 2025, filed at Companies House on 25 July 2026 (74 pages) - the single best primary check on the '$90m of EBITDA-accretive revenue' claim - could not be retrieved: the document endpoint 302s to a signed AWS S3 URL that could not be followed, the xhtml variant 500s, and Endole/Pomanda both 403. The only publicly quoted turnover figure, £52.89m, is ambiguously attributed between FY-Apr-2024 and FY-Apr-2025 by aggregators, so I dropped it rather than guess. This is the highest-value unread document on the name.
Trade receivables / DSO for 2026 - no post-31-Dec-2025 receivables datum exists anywhere; the sweep's DSO idea is only testable after the print, not before it
Any Crownpeak refinancing, extension or replacement of the 31 December 2026 term loans - nothing announced in any 6-K, press release or UK filing
Crownpeak customer churn, WARN notices or layoffs post-acquisition; Glassdoor and headcount trackers show ~183 employees and nothing anomalous

Whether Rezolve intends to revive its rejected 1-for-2 exchange offer for Commerce.com at the 1 September call - the 6 August 6-K/425 pair says only that it 'remains open' on revised terms, which is not a datable event
Rezolve India headcount corroboration for the '550 specialists' claim (no Indian MCA filing or job-posting count found that either supports or contradicts it)
Auditor change: no 6-K, 20-F item or press release naming a successor to Grassi & Co for FY2026, despite the July 2026 auditor-appointment resolution
Any actual buyback execution to date - none; the mandate is still pre-court-approval
Insider selling ahead of the print: the only Form 4 (28 Aug 2026) is a non-market option exercise and estate distribution inside the CEO's DBLP vehicle, no open-market sales
baseline_tension: The baseline has no directional statement to agree or disagree with - 25-delta skew is null and there are zero prior reactions - so the two things it does say are the ones I cut against: a +16.8% five-day run-up and front-expiry open interest that is four-to-one calls over puts describe a book positioned for the 1 September print to confirm the $127m and start the $300m buyback, while the only genuinely new information in the report is the balance sheet that bounds the buyback at a fraction of that; the 12.04% implied move is honest about how wide the outcome is, and my -4.0 is deliberately well inside it because this management has surged the stock off its own results release before.
